title: Descending degeneracy corrections preserve lower faces and realize upper faces
statement: Let $G:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be a simplicial abelian group with face homomorphisms $d_i$ and degeneracy homomorphisms $s_i$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Let $n\geq2$, $0\leq k\leq n$, and let $a_i\in G_{n-1}$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, $i\ne k$, satisfy $d_i a_j=d_{j-1}a_i$ for $i<j$ with $i,j\ne k$. Suppose $v\in G_n$ satisfies $d_iv=a_i$ for all $i<k$. Define $w_n=v$ and, in descending order for $n\geq r>k$, $$b_r=a_r-d_rw_r,\qquad w_{r-1}=w_r+s_{r-1}b_r.$$ For every $k\leq r\leq n$ one has $d_iw_r=a_i$ whenever $i<k$ or $r<i\leq n$. In addition, at every $r>k$, $d_i b_r=0$ and $d_i(s_{r-1}b_r)=0$ for $i<k$, while $d_{i-1}b_r=0$ and $d_i(s_{r-1}b_r)=0$ for $r<i\leq n$, and $d_r(s_{r-1}b_r)=b_r$. When $k=n$ the sequence consists only of $w_n=v$; when $k=0$ all lower-face assertions are empty.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, third paragraph (lines 5788-5803): the descending upper-face correction induction and preservation of the previously fixed lower faces, specialized additively.

proof.text: By the definition of the face operators, applying the contravariant functor $G$ to the simplex face-face identity gives $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$ for $i<j$. All these operators are homomorphisms, since $G$ takes values in $\mathrm{Ab}$, so they preserve zero, sums and differences.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, third paragraph (lines 5788-5803): the descending upper-face correction induction and preservation of the previously fixed lower faces, specialized additively.

proof.text: Induct downwards on $r$ from $n$ to $k$, with invariant $P(r)$: $d_iw_r=a_i$ for $i<k$ and for $r<i\leq n$. At $r=n$ the upper range is empty, and the lower assertions are exactly the hypothesis on $v=w_n$. The recursion defines the finitely many remaining $w_r$ because $r>k\geq0$ makes $s_{r-1}:G_{n-1}\to G_n$ a valid operator.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, third paragraph (lines 5788-5803): the descending upper-face correction induction and preservation of the previously fixed lower faces, specialized additively.

proof.text: Assume $P(r)$ with $r>k$ and set $b_r=a_r-d_rw_r$. For $i<k$ we have $i<r$ and both $i,r\ne k$; compatibility and Step 1 give $$d_i b_r=d_i a_r-d_i d_rw_r=d_{r-1}a_i-d_{r-1}d_iw_r=0.$$ For $r<i\leq n$ both $r,i\ne k$; the same compatibility with the pair $(r,i)$ gives $$d_{i-1}b_r=d_{i-1}a_r-d_{i-1}d_rw_r=d_ra_i-d_rd_iw_r=0.$$ These are exactly the asserted defect vanishings.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, third paragraph (lines 5788-5803): the descending upper-face correction induction and preservation of the previously fixed lower faces, specialized additively.

proof.text: Use the mixed identities with degeneracy index $r-1$. For $i<k$, necessarily $i<r-1$, so $d_i(s_{r-1}b_r)=s_{r-2}(d_i b_r)=0$. This case occurs only when $r\geq2$; if $r=1$, then $k=0$ and the lower range is empty, so $s_{-1}$ is never used. For $r<i\leq n$, $i>(r-1)+1$, hence $d_i(s_{r-1}b_r)=s_{r-1}(d_{i-1}b_r)=0$. Finally the adjacent identity gives $d_r(s_{r-1}b_r)=b_r$. Here we used Step 3 and preservation of zero by homomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, third paragraph (lines 5788-5803): the descending upper-face correction induction and preservation of the previously fixed lower faces, specialized additively.

proof.text: For $w_{r-1}=w_r+s_{r-1}b_r$, Step 4 and additivity give $d_iw_{r-1}=a_i+0=a_i$ for $i<k$ and for $i>r$, while $$d_rw_{r-1}=d_rw_r+b_r=d_rw_r+(a_r-d_rw_r)=a_r.$$ Thus $P(r-1)$ holds. Finite descending induction proves all $P(r)$, and Steps 3 and 4 prove all additional assertions at each correction.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, third paragraph (lines 5788-5803): the descending upper-face correction induction and preservation of the previously fixed lower faces, specialized additively.

proof.text: If $k=n$, there are no correction indices and only $w_n=v$ remains, with the asserted invariant supplied by the hypothesis. If $k=0$, all lower-face ranges in the preceding argument are empty; the upper-face calculation and the adjacent identity still apply, including the final correction $r=1$ using $s_0$.

lean.statement: theorem abelianDescendingCorrection_spec (G : SimplicialObject AddCommGrpCat.{u}) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin (m + 3)) (a : (i : Fin (m + 3)) → i ≠ k → G _⦋m + 1⦌) (ha : ∀ (i j : Fin (m + 2)), i ≤ j → ∀ (hi : i.castSucc ≠ k) (hj : j.succ ≠ k), G.δ i (a j.succ hj) = G.δ j (a i.castSucc hi)) (v : G _⦋m + 2⦌) (hv : ∀ (i : Fin (m + 3)), i < k → ∀ (hi : i ≠ k), G.δ i v = a i hi) : abelianDescendingCorrection G k a v (m + 2) = v ∧ (∀ (r : Fin (m + 3)), k ≤ r → ∀ (i : Fin (m + 3)), i < k ∨ r < i → ∀ (hi : i ≠ k), G.δ i (abelianDescendingCorrection G k a v r.val) = a i hi) ∧ (∀ (r : Fin (m + 3)) (hr : k < r), (∀ (i : Fin (m + 2)), i.val < k.val → G.δ i (abelianDescendingDefect G k a v r hr) = 0 ∧ G.δ i.castSucc (G.σ ⟨r.val - 1, by omega⟩ (abelianDescendingDefect G k a v r hr)) = 0) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin (m + 3)), r < i → G.δ ⟨i.val - 1, by omega⟩ (abelianDescendingDefect G k a v r hr) = 0 ∧ G.δ i (G.σ ⟨r.val - 1, by omega⟩ (abelianDescendingDefect G k a v r hr)) = 0) ∧ G.δ r (G.σ ⟨r.val - 1, by omega⟩ (abelianDescendingDefect G k a v r hr)) = abelianDescendingDefect G k a v r hr)
